reviewer_note: Adversarial re-verification of round-3's two AMBER findings (E-001 P1 QR-logo safety margin, E-002 P2 account-title contrast), followed by a full fresh regression sweep. Did NOT trust either fix agent's summary: re-derived E-001's CSS state by direct grep on both blade files; independently authored a NEW degradation pipeline (PHP GD downscale+upscale, gaussian blur, JPEG recompress at graduated severities) rather than re-running or reading the fix agent's own degradation script, and probed logo widths 20/22/26% at 11 severity combinations plus a pure-lossless check at 8 widths (20-36%); re-derived E-002 by reading styles.css directly, computing getComputedStyle() live in-browser on both affected states, and visually inspecting fresh screenshots (Read tool). Backend HEAD moved from round-3's ed9f88d69 through b4e8b29de (E-001 fix) plus 6 further concurrent-session commits on borne.blade.php (portrait-layout iteration, culminating in the wheel being hidden in portrait after 4 failed layout attempts) to final HEAD 27d4d7712, all reviewed for scope. Web repo HEAD moved from round-3's 27b56e5 to 416c798 (E-002 fix only, no other drift).

findings.evidence: E-001's fix commit (b4e8b29de) claims: 'à 26% le décodage échoue sur 2/4 variantes, dont exactement celle qui décode sans problème à 20%' (at 26% decode fails on 2/4 degraded variants, including exactly the one that decodes fine at 20%). Built an independently-authored degradation pipeline (GD downscale+upscale + imagefilter(IMG_FILTER_GAUSSIAN_BLUR) x1-4 passes + imagejpeg recompress q20-60) and tested clean, isolated, single-fresh-page-load captures (avoiding a contamination artifact discovered mid-probe: re-using one page across 8 sequential CSS-override+screenshot iterations produced spuriously undecodable base PNGs for ALL widths, even 20% lossless — root-caused to page-reuse timing, not logo width; redone with one fresh page/PIN-unlock per width to get clean data) at widths 20%, 22%, 26% across 7 severity combinations from mild to extreme. Result: at 6 of 7 combinations, all three widths behaved IDENTICALLY (all-pass or all-fail together) — no width-dependent effect at all. At the one combination that showed ANY split (scale=0.2, gaussian-blur x3, JPEG q25), the result was the OPPOSITE of the fix commit's claim: 20% and 22% FAILED to decode (3/3 repeats each, deterministic) while 26% PASSED (3/3 repeats). Lossless (undegraded) decode passed at every width tested from 20% up to 36%, consistent with round-3's own finding of 'no proven real-world scan failure today'. Conclusion: the specific causal narrative in b4e8b29de (26% measurably less safe than 20% under realistic degradation) is NOT independently reproducible — it appears to be an artifact of that script's own particular degradation recipe interacting incidentally with pixel alignment, not a robust, width-driven safety boundary. Decode success/failure in both pipelines is dominated by overall image-quality severity, not by the 6-point difference in logo coverage within the 20-26% band.
findings.fix_hint: No code change needed — the ACTUAL fix (reverting borne.blade.php's .qr-logo to 20%) is independently justifiable on other grounds already established pre-round-4 (matches the spec's own validated-safe ceiling of 22%, matches validation.blade.php's sibling markup, zero regression risk since lossless decode was already proven safe at both 20% and 26%). Recommend only a documentation correction: soften or remove the specific 'fails 2/4 variants at 26%, passes 4/4 at 20%' causal claim from the commit message/comments, since it is not corroborated and a future reader could over-trust it as an established physical safety boundary. If a future degraded-condition probe is meant to be authoritative, commit its exact methodology (not just its conclusion) to the repo so it is independently reproducible.

convergence_status: NOT DECLARED YET — explicit reasoned call, see below. Round 4 itself is clean: 0 open P0/P1/P2, both round-3 findings independently re-verified closed (one with a P3 evidence-quality caveat on E-001's stated rationale, not on its code correctness), full 8-suite regression green, frozen zones untouched. However, this is judged to be the FIRST clean round on E-001/E-002, not the second: round-2's GREEN verdict was against the ORIGINAL 6 findings and never examined E-001/E-002 (they did not exist yet as findings), so it provides no evidence of E-001/E-002's fix STABILITY — the two-consecutive-clean-round discipline exists specifically to catch fixes that look right once but regress or were coincidentally green, and round-2's cleanliness cannot be borrowed to satisfy that for a different pair of findings it never tested. Two further concrete reasons tip this toward 'not yet' rather than a borderline call: (1) borne.blade.php — the exact file E-001 lived in — received SIX more concurrent-session commits during the round-3→round-4 window alone, confirmed unrelated to `.qr-logo` this time, but demonstrating the drift risk that caused E-001 is ONGOING and live, not historical; declaring convergence now judges a moving target as settled. (2) This round's own independent adversarial reproduction (F-001) could not corroborate E-001's stated safety mechanism, even though the resulting code state is verified safe — that lowers confidence in E-001 specifically enough to want one more untroubled confirmation pass before calling it closed for good. RECOMMENDATION: run a round 5 as a lightweight confirmation (re-check `.qr-logo` still 20% on both files, re-run the 8-suite regression list, spot-check any further borne.blade.php churn for `.qr-logo` collateral) rather than a full fresh audit — if round 5 is clean with zero new findings, that constitutes genuine two-consecutive-clean evidence and convergence should be declared then.
